    45  /-- What kind of constant a name is stored as. -/
    46  inductive ConstKind where
    47    /-- A definition: its value unfolds (δ). -/
    48    | defn (value : Expr)
    49    /-- An inductive type former with `numParams` parameters,

    54    | ctor (induct : Name) (numParams nfields : Nat)

    57    `numIndices` indices, then the major premise — and its rules. -/
    58    | recursor (numParams numMotives numMinors numIndices : Nat) (rules : List RecRule)

== whitepaper/Fragment/Decl.lean#L395-L405
   395  /-- **A definition is accepted** (con-leche's `checkDefnVal`): the
   396  name is fresh, the declared type's type reduces to a sort, the
   397  value's inferred type is definitionally equal to the declared type,
   398  and both terms are in scope (closed, stored constants, declared level
   399  parameters). -/
   400  def DefOk (env : Env) (c : Name) (ci : ConstInfo) : Prop :=
   401    env.find? c = none ∧
   402    (∃ s u, Infer env [] ci.type s ∧ Red env [] s (.sort u)) ∧
   403    (∃ v T, ci.kind = .defn v ∧ Infer env [] v T ∧ DefEq env [] T ci.type ∧
   404      Expr.Scoped env ci.lparams 0 v) ∧
   405    Expr.Scoped env ci.lparams 0 ci.type

== ConLeche/Kernel/Checker.lean#L36-L52
    36  def checkDefnVal (ops : CheckerOps m) (env : Env) (cv : ConstantVal)
    37      (value : Expr) (hint : ReducibilityHint) : m Env := do
    38    unless value.looseBVarsBounded 0 do
    39      throw (.invalid s!"loose bound variable in value of {cv.name}")
    40    if value.hasFvar then
    41      throw (.invalid s!"unexpected free variable in value of {cv.name}")
    42    let value ← ops.annotate env 0 value
    43    unless value.allLevelParamsDefined cv.levelParams do
    44      throw (.invalid s!"undeclared universe parameter in value of {cv.name}")
    45    unless value.constsResolve env do
    46      throw (unresolvedConstsError s!"value of {cv.name}" value)
    47    let vtype ← ops.inferType env 0 value
    48    unless ← ops.isDefEq env 0 vtype cv.type do
    49      throw (.invalid s!"type mismatch in definition {cv.name}")
    50    pure ⟨.defnInfo cv value hint :: env.consts⟩
    51  
    52  /-- Check a `theorem` declaration's value against its checked constant

   386  def Scoped (env : Env) (ps : List Name) (k : Nat) (e : Expr) : Prop :=
   387    e.closedAt k = true ∧ (∀ c ∈ e.consts, (env.find? c).isSome) ∧ e.lparamsIn ps = true

== whitepaper/Fragment/EnvModel.lean#L163-L189
   163  /-- **A model of an environment**: the assignment and the three laws. -/
   164  structure EnvModel (V : Type u) [SetLib V] (env : Env) where
   165    /-- The set of every constant at every list of concrete levels. -/
   166    M : Name → List Nat → V
   167    /-- Every stored constant's type, instantiated, is well-denoted, and
   168    the constant is a member of it — at every valuation and every
   169    environment (the types are closed, so `ρ` is irrelevant, and stating
   170    it for all `ρ` saves a closedness lemma). -/
   171    type_ok : ∀ (c : Name) (ci : ConstInfo), env.find? c = some ci →
   172      ∀ (φ : Name → Nat) (ρ : Nat → V) (ls : List Level), ls.length = ci.lparams.length →
   173        WellDenoted M φ ρ (ci.type.instL ci.lparams ls) ∧
   174        M c (ls.map (Level.eval φ)) ∈ˢ interp M φ ρ (ci.type.instL ci.lparams ls)
   175    /-- A definition's value, instantiated, is well-denoted and denotes
   176    the constant. -/
   177    unfold : ∀ (c : Name) (ci : ConstInfo) (v : Expr), env.find? c = some ci →
   178      ci.value? = some v →
   179      ∀ (φ : Name → Nat) (ρ : Nat → V) (ls : List Level), ls.length = ci.lparams.length →
   180        WellDenoted M φ ρ (v.instL ci.lparams ls) ∧
   181        interp M φ ρ (v.instL ci.lparams ls) = M c (ls.map (Level.eval φ))
   182    /-- Every rule of every stored recursor satisfies its ι law. -/
   183    rec_rules : ∀ (c : Name) (ci : ConstInfo) (numParams numMotives numMinors numIndices : Nat)
   184      (rules : List RecRule),
   185      env.find? c = some ci →
   186      ci.kind = .recursor numParams numMotives numMinors numIndices rules →
   187      ∀ rl ∈ rules, ∀ cij : ConstInfo, env.find? rl.ctor = some cij →
   188        RecRuleLaw M c ci numParams (numParams + numMotives + numMinors)
   189          (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices) rl cij

== whitepaper/Fragment/Decl.lean#L129-L142
   129  /-- A constructor field, as the positivity check classifies it
   130  (con-leche's `RecFieldKind`, `NativeParts.lean:51`).  Its domain is an
   131  expression under the parameters and the earlier fields. -/
   132  inductive Field where
   133    /-- An ordinary field: any domain that does not mention the block. -/
   134    | ordinary (A : Expr)
   135    /-- A recursive field: the family at the block's parameters and the
   136    index expressions `es` (a spine, outermost first). -/
   137    | recursive (es : List Expr)
   138    /-- A reflexive field: `∀ tele, I params es` — a function space into
   139    the family; `tele` is a context (innermost first) under the
   140    parameters and the earlier fields, `es` a spine under `tele` too. -/
   141    | reflexive (tele : List Expr) (es : List Expr)
   142    deriving DecidableEq

== ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/NativeParts.lean#L62-L70
    62  inductive RecFieldKind where
    63    /-- the domain does not mention the block -/
    64    | ordinary
    65    /-- the domain is exactly `T p⃗ e⃗`: a finitary recursive field -/
    66    | recursive
    67    /-- the domain is `Π a⃗ : A⃗, T p⃗ e⃗(a⃗)` with `A⃗` free of the block: a
    68    REFLEXIVE (function-space) recursive field (task #202) -/
    69    | reflexive
    70    /-- a non-positive (or non-valid) occurrence: the official kernel

== whitepaper/Fragment/Decl.lean#L411-L424
   411  /-- The scope of a field's pieces: with `k` earlier fields, an
   412  ordinary domain is in scope under the parameters and them; a recursive
   413  field's index expressions too; a reflexive field's telescope entries
   414  under the earlier telescope entries as well, and its index
   415  expressions under the whole telescope.  No piece mentions the block
   416  (it is not stored in `env`): that is **strict positivity** in the
   417  shape the fragment admits (con-leche's `recPositivity`,
   418  `NativeParts.lean:89`). -/
   419  def fieldScoped (env : Env) (k : Nat) : Field → Prop
   420    | .ordinary A => Expr.Scoped env S.lparams (S.nP + k) A
   421    | .recursive es => ∀ e ∈ es, Expr.Scoped env S.lparams (S.nP + k) e
   422    | .reflexive tele es =>
   423      (∀ t T, tele[t]? = some T → Expr.Scoped env S.lparams (S.nP + k + (tele.length - 1 - t)) T) ∧
   424      (∀ e ∈ es, Expr.Scoped env S.lparams (S.nP + k + tele.length) e)

== ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/NativeParts.lean#L97-L113
    97  def recPositivity (T : Name) (lps : List Name) (nP nIdx o : Nat) : Expr → Nat → RecFieldKind
    98    | .forallE dom body _, k =>
    99      if dom.mentionsConst T then .negative else recPositivity T lps nP nIdx o body (k + 1)
   100    | e, k =>
   101      if !e.mentionsConst T then .ordinary
   102      else if e.getAppFn == Expr.const T (lps.map .param) then
   103        if e.getAppArgs.length == nP + nIdx && e.getAppArgs.take nP == structPsAt (o + k) nP then
   104          (if recFamOk T lps nP nIdx (o + k) e then
   105            (if k == 0 then .recursive else .reflexive)
   106           else .negative)
   107        else .negative
   108      else
   109        match e.getAppFn with
   110        | .const T' _ => if T' == T then .negative else .unsupported
   111        | _ => .unsupported

== whitepaper/Fragment/Decl.lean#L277-L290
   277  /-- **An inductive hypothesis' type** for the field with `k` earlier
   278  fields, `l` earlier hypotheses, `o` binders between the parameters
   279  and the fields (the motive sits `nF + l + o - 1` binders above):
   280  `motive es f` at a recursive field, `∀ tele, motive es (f tele)` at a
   281  reflexive one. -/
   282  def ihTy (nF k l o : Nat) : Field → Expr
   283    | .ordinary _ => .sort .zero
   284    | .recursive es =>
   285      mkAppN (.bvar (nF + l + o - 1)) (es.map (atCtx nF k l o 0) ++ [.bvar (nF - 1 - k + l)])
   286    | .reflexive tele es =>
   287      let m := tele.length
   288      mkPis S.q (liftCtx (fun t T => atCtx nF k l o t T) tele)
   289        (mkAppN (.bvar (nF + l + o - 1 + m))
   290          (es.map (atCtx nF k l o m) ++ [mkAppN (.bvar (nF - 1 - k + l + m)) (varsAt 0 m)]))

   450  /-- **The subsingleton criterion** for a field of sort `v` at

   124  def checkStructFieldSortsI (ops : CheckerOps m) (env : Env) (isProp large : Bool)
   125      (s : Level) (nP : Nat) (fvs idxArgs : List Expr) : Nat → m (List Level)
   126    | 0 => pure []
   127    | j + 1 => do

   136          throw (.invalid "direct sum: large eliminator with a non-propositional \

   138      let rest ← checkStructFieldSortsI ops env isProp large s nP fvs idxArgs j

   439  /-- The universe bound on a field of sort `v`: the family is a
   440  proposition, or `v ≤ u` (official's "universe level of `type_of(arg)`

== whitepaper/Fragment/Decl.lean#L459-L492
   459  /-- **The block is accepted** (con-leche's `checkNative`,
   460  `NativeInstall.lean:617`):
   461  
   462  * the block's names are distinct and fresh;
   463  * the specification is in scope (closed, stored constants, declared
   464    level parameters — positivity included);
   465  * the generated type former's type has a sort in the current
   466    environment;
   467  * each generated constructor's type has a sort in the environment
   468    holding the former, and every field's domain has a sort respecting
   469    the universe bound and, where a large eliminator asks it, the
   470    subsingleton criterion;
   471  * a large eliminator on a block whose sort may be `Prop` has at most
   472    one constructor (official's `elim_only_at_universe_zero`);
   473  * the generated recursor's type has a sort in the environment holding
   474    the former and the constructors.
   475  
   476  The recursor's rules are generated and stored, not checked: they
   477  mention the recursor, and con-leche does not infer them either
   478  (`NativeInstall.lean`, "the rules … are scope-checked at the
   479  environment holding its constant and NOT inferred"). -/
   480  def Ok (env : Env) : Prop :=
   481    (S.name :: S.recName :: S.ctors.map (·.name)).Nodup ∧
   482    (∀ m ∈ S.name :: S.recName :: S.ctors.map (·.name), env.find? m = none) ∧
   483    S.Scoped env ∧
   484    (∃ T, Infer env [] S.indType T) ∧
   485    (∀ c ∈ S.ctors,
   486      (∃ T, Infer (S.envInd env) [] (S.ctorType c) T) ∧
   487      (∀ i A, (S.fieldCtx c.fields)[i]? = some A →
   488        ∃ s v, Infer (S.envInd env) ((S.fieldCtx c.fields).drop (i + 1) ++ S.params) A s ∧
   489          Red (S.envInd env) ((S.fieldCtx c.fields).drop (i + 1) ++ S.params) s (.sort v) ∧
   490          S.FieldBound v ∧ S.SubsingletonField v i c.idx)) ∧
   491    (S.large = true → ¬ S.NeverProp → S.ctors.length ≤ 1) ∧
   492    (∃ T, Infer (S.envCtors env) [] S.recType T)

== whitepaper/Fragment/IndLib.lean#L50-L78
    50  /-- **The library for inductive types**: `SetLib` with separation,
    51  transitivity, tuples and tags. -/
    52  class IndLib (V : Type u) extends SetLib V where
    53    /-- Separation: the members of `A` that satisfy `P`. -/
    54    sep : V → (V → Prop) → V
    55    /-- The members of a separation. -/
    56    mem_sep : ∀ {A : V} {P : V → Prop} {x : V}, Mem x (sep A P) ↔ Mem x A ∧ P x
    57    /-- A separated part of a member of a positive universe is a member of
    58    it. -/
    59    sep_mem_univ : ∀ {n : Nat} {A : V} {P : V → Prop}, n ≠ 0 →
    60      Mem A (univ n) → Mem (sep A P) (univ n)
    61    /-- The positive universes are transitive: a member of a member is a
    62    member. -/
    63    univ_trans : ∀ {n : Nat} {A x : V}, n ≠ 0 → Mem A (univ n) → Mem x A → Mem x (univ n)
    64    /-- The n-ary tuple of a list of sets. -/
    65    tuple : List V → V
    66    /-- Tuples are injective. -/
    67    tuple_inj : ∀ {xs ys : List V}, tuple xs = tuple ys → xs = ys
    68    /-- A tuple of members of a positive universe is a member of it. -/
    69    tuple_mem_univ : ∀ {n : Nat} {xs : List V}, n ≠ 0 →
    70      (∀ x ∈ xs, Mem x (univ n)) → Mem (tuple xs) (univ n)
    71    /-- A value tagged with a number. -/
    72    tag : Nat → V → V
    73    /-- Tags are injective. -/
    74    tag_inj : ∀ {i j : Nat} {x y : V}, tag i x = tag j y → i = j ∧ x = y
    75    /-- A tagged member of a positive universe is a member of it. -/
    76    tag_mem_univ : ∀ {n i : Nat} {x : V}, n ≠ 0 → Mem x (univ n) → Mem (tag i x) (univ n)
    77    /-- A tagged value is never the point. -/
    78    tag_ne_pt : ∀ {i : Nat} {x : V}, tag i x ≠ pt

== whitepaper/Fragment/IndLib.lean#L138-L141
   138  /-- **The least fixed point** of an operator on predicates: the
   139  intersection of every predicate closed under it. -/
   140  def Lfp {α : Sort _} (Φ : (α → Prop) → (α → Prop)) : α → Prop :=
   141    fun a => ∀ P : α → Prop, (∀ b, Φ P b → P b) → P a

== whitepaper/Fragment/IndLib.lean#L147-L165
   147  /-- The least fixed point is below every closed predicate. -/
   148  theorem least {P : α → Prop} (h : ∀ b, Φ P b → P b) {a : α} (ha : Lfp Φ a) : P a :=
   149    ha P h
   150  
   151  /-- The least fixed point is closed. -/
   152  theorem closed (hm : Mono Φ) {a : α} (h : Φ (Lfp Φ) a) : Lfp Φ a :=
   153    fun P hP => hP a (hm _ _ (fun _ hb => hb P hP) a h)
   154  
   155  /-- The least fixed point is a fixed point: a member is a step from
   156  members. -/
   157  theorem unfold (hm : Mono Φ) {a : α} (h : Lfp Φ a) : Φ (Lfp Φ) a :=
   158    h (fun b => Φ (Lfp Φ) b) fun b hb => hm _ _ (fun _ hc => closed hm hc) b hb
   159  
   160  /-- **Induction**: a property that holds at every step from members
   161  that have it (and are members) holds on the least fixed point. -/
   162  theorem induction (hm : Mono Φ) {P : α → Prop}
   163      (h : ∀ b, Φ (fun c => Lfp Φ c ∧ P c) b → P b) {a : α} (ha : Lfp Φ a) : P a :=
   164    (least (P := fun c => Lfp Φ c ∧ P c)
   165      (fun b hb => ⟨closed hm (hm _ _ (fun _ hc => hc.1) b hb), h b hb⟩) ha).2

    65  /-- **The least pre-fixed family of `F` over `I`** — fibrewise the
    66  intersection of the closed families when there is one (separated from

    68  noncomputable def lfpFamSet (w : Nat) (I F : V) : V :=

    70      graph (fun i => sep (app (Classical.choose h) i)
    71        (fun x => ∀ X, IsClosedFam w I F X → x ∈ˢ app X i)) I

== ConLeche/SetModel/Iter.lean#L8-L24
     8  # The ω-iterate of a set functor (task #188)
     9  
    10  The one place iteration survives in the recursive-type model: the
    11  carrier is the Knaster–Tarski least pre-fixed point
    12  (`ConLeche/SetTheory/Derive/Lfp.lean`), and every law about it assumes a
    13  CLOSED MEMBER of the universe exists.  For a *finitary* tower functor
    14  that witness is the ω-iterate
    15  
    16      iterF Φ 0 = ∅,   iterF Φ (n+1) = Φ (iterF Φ n),   iterU Φ = ⋃ₙ iterF Φ n
    17  
    18  — a countable union of members of `univ w`, hence a member (`ω ∈ univ
    19  w` at `w ≥ 1`, `omega_mem_univ_succ`; at `w = 0` truth values), and
    20  closed under `Φ` whenever every member of `Φ (iterU Φ)` already lies in
    21  some `Φ (iterF Φ n)` (`iterU_closed_of` — the finitary condition,
    22  discharged for the tower functor in `ConLeche/Semantics/Tower/FixLeaf.lean`
    23  by bounding the ranks of a tuple's finitely many recursive fields).
    24  The union is also where the recursor's semantic fixed point is built

== whitepaper/Fragment/EnvModel.lean#L60-L67
    60  /-- **Semantic fit of values to a telescope**: each value is a member
    61  of the domain it meets, the body read under the values so far
    62  (`TeleFit` with the arguments' denotations in place of the arguments
    63  — the environment grows instead of the type being substituted into). -/
    64  def TeleFitV (M : Name → List Nat → V) (φ : Name → Nat) : (Nat → V) → Expr → List V → Prop
    65    | _, _, [] => True
    66    | ρ, .pi A _ B, v :: vs => v ∈ˢ interp M φ ρ A ∧ TeleFitV M φ (cons v ρ) B vs
    67    | _, _, _ :: _ => False

   114  /-- The function space is monotone in its fibres. -/
   115  theorem piSet_mono {A : V} {B B' : V → V} (h : ∀ x, x ∈ˢ A → B x ⊆ˢ B' x) :
   116      piSet A B ⊆ˢ piSet A B' := by
   117    intro f hf
   118    rw [← graph_app_eq hf]
   119    exact graph_mem_piSet fun x hx => h x hx _ (app_mem_piSet hf hx)
   120  
   121  /-- The two-regime product is monotone in its fibres. -/
   122  theorem piR_mono {p : Bool} {A : V} {B B' : V → V} (h : ∀ x, x ∈ˢ A → B x ⊆ˢ B' x) :
   123      piR p A B ⊆ˢ piR p A B' := by
   124    cases p
   125    · exact piSet_mono h
   126    · intro f hf
   127      obtain ⟨rfl, hi⟩ := mem_truthVal.mp hf
   128      exact pt_mem_truthVal fun x hx => (hi x hx).imp fun y hy => h x hx y hy

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L84-L156
    84    /-- **ι** (`Red.iota`, `Rel.lean:184`): a stored recursor applied to
    85    exactly its telescope — `numParams` parameters, `numMotives` motives,
    86    `numMinors` minor premises, `numIndices` indices and the major
    87    premise — whose major reduces to a constructor application with a
    88    rule, fires the rule: the rule's right-hand side, at the use's
    89    levels, applied to the parameters, motives and minors, then to the
    90    constructor's fields (its arguments after the parameters).
    91  
    92    The two **telescope certificates** are `Rel.lean`'s `Certs` walks
    93    (`:576-587`) folded in: the recursor's argument spine (with the
    94    reduced major) and the constructor's argument spine are each typed
    95    against the stored type's `Π`-telescope — every argument's type is
    96    inferred and found definitionally equal to the binder domain it
    97    meets (`Expr.piDomains`), and the stored type has the spine's
    98    length of syntactic binders (`Expr.hasPis`; a generated type does).
    99    They are what makes the environment's ι law (`EnvModel.lean`,
   100    `RecRuleLaw`) applicable: they put every argument in its domain.
   101  
   102    The **three comparisons** after them are `Rel.lean`'s too
   103    (`:206-231`): the constructor's levels are the recursor's (its last
   104    `usj.length` ones — a large eliminator carries one extra level in
   105    front), the constructor's parameters are definitionally the
   106    recursor's, and the constructor's residual type
   107    (`Expr.piResidual`: the family at the constructor's own parameters
   108    and index expressions, with the fields substituted in) has index
   109    expressions definitionally equal to the recursor's index arguments.
   110    In the model they matter exactly when the family is a proposition:
   111    there the major denotes the one point, the certificates say only
   112    that the fibre is inhabited, and the fields the rule's right-hand
   113    side receives can be related to the recursor's own parameters and
   114    indices through these comparisons alone (`Install.lean`). -/
   115    | iota {Γ : List Expr} {c : Name} {us : List Level} {ci : ConstInfo}
   116        {numParams numMotives numMinors numIndices : Nat} {rules : List RecRule}
   117        {args : List Expr} {major : Expr} {cj : Name} {usj : List Level}
   118        {cij : ConstInfo} {margs : List Expr} {rl : RecRule}
   119        {doms tys doms' tys' : List Expr}
   120        {residual : Expr} {I : Name} {lsI : List Level} {rps ridx : List Expr} :
   121        env.find? c = some ci →
   122        ci.kind = .recursor numParams numMotives numMinors numIndices rules →
   123        us.length = ci.lparams.length →
   124        args.length = numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices + 1 →
   125        ci.type.hasPis (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices + 1) = true →
   126        Red env Γ (args.getD (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices) (bvar 0))
   127          major →
   128        major = mkAppN (const cj usj) margs →
   129        rl ∈ rules → rl.ctor = cj →
   130        env.find? cj = some cij →
   131        usj.length = cij.lparams.length →
   132        margs.length = numParams + rl.nfields →
   133        cij.type.hasPis (numParams + rl.nfields) = true →
   134        -- the recursor's telescope certificate, on the spine with the reduced major
   135        piDomains (ci.type.instL ci.lparams us)
   136          (args.take (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices) ++ [major]) = some doms →
   137        tys.length = doms.length →
   138        (∀ p ∈ (args.take (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices) ++ [major]).zip tys,
   139          Infer env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   140        (∀ p ∈ tys.zip doms, DefEq env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   141        -- the constructor's telescope certificate
   142        piDomains (cij.type.instL cij.lparams usj) margs = some doms' →
   143        tys'.length = doms'.length →
   144        (∀ p ∈ margs.zip tys', Infer env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   145        (∀ p ∈ tys'.zip doms', DefEq env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   146        -- the constructor's levels, parameters and residual indices against the recursor's
   147        Level.eqList usj (us.drop (us.length - usj.length)) = true →
   148        (∀ p ∈ (margs.take numParams).zip (args.take numParams), DefEq env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   149        piResidual (cij.type.instL cij.lparams usj) margs = some residual →
   150        residual = mkAppN (const I lsI) (rps ++ ridx) →
   151        rps.length = numParams →
   152        (∀ p ∈ ridx.zip ((args.take (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices)).drop
   153          (numParams + numMotives + numMinors)), DefEq env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   154        Red env Γ (mkAppN (const c us) args)
   155          (mkAppN (rl.rhs.instL ci.lparams us)
   156            (args.take (numParams + numMotives + numMinors) ++ margs.drop numParams))

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L179-L224
   179    applied to exactly its telescope, whose prepared major (the `Red`
   180    premise: `prepareMajor`'s whnf / literal / rescue chain) is a
   181    constructor application with a firing rule.  The level comparands,
   182    the parameter comparison, the two licensed telescope certificates
   183    and the index comparison are the checker's, in its order. -/
   184    | iota {d : Nat} {e : Expr} {c : Name} {us : List Level} {cv : ConstantVal}
   185        {mI rP : Nat} {rules : List RecRule} {major : Expr} {cj : Name}
   186        {usj : List Level} {cvj : ConstantVal} {cnP cnF : Nat} {rl : RecRule}
   187        {residual : Expr} :
   188        e.getAppFn = .const c us →
   189        env.find? c = some (.recInfo cv mI rP rules) →
   190        e.getAppArgs.length = mI + 1 →
   191        us.length = cv.levelParams.length →
   192        Red env d (e.getAppArgs.getD mI (.bvar 0)) major →
   193        major.getAppFn = .const cj usj →
   194        env.find? cj = some (.ctorInfo cvj cnP cnF) →
   195        rules.find? (fun r' => r'.ctor == cj) = some rl →
   196        major.getAppArgs.length = rl.ctorParams + rl.nfields →
   197        rl.fire ≠ .inert →
   198        Level.isEquivList usj
   199          (recFireComparands rl cv.levelParams us cvj.levelParams
   200            e.getAppArgs rP).1 = some true →
   201        (rl.compareParams = true →
   202          DefEqList env d (major.getAppArgs.take rl.ctorParams)
   203            (recFireComparands rl cv.levelParams us cvj.levelParams
   204              e.getAppArgs rP).2) →
   205        Certs env d true (cv.type.instantiateLevelParams cv.levelParams us)
   206          (e.getAppArgs.take mI ++ [major]) →
   207        Certs env d true (cvj.type.instantiateLevelParams cvj.levelParams usj)
   208          major.getAppArgs →
   209        (mI ≠ rP →
   210          piResidual (cvj.type.instantiateLevelParams cvj.levelParams usj)
   211            major.getAppArgs = some residual) →
   212        (mI ≠ rP →
   213          DefEqList env d (residual.getAppArgs.drop rl.ctorParams)
   214            ((e.getAppArgs.take mI).drop rP)) →
   215        Red env d e
   216          (Expr.mkAppN (rl.rhs.instantiateLevelParams cv.levelParams us)
   217            (e.getAppArgs.take rP ++ major.getAppArgs.drop rl.ctorParams))
   218    /-- **The K rescue** (`majorToCtor`'s K branch, `Core.lean:570-620`;
   219    official `to_cnstr_when_K`): at a K-flagged single-rule recursor the
   220    parameters-only constructor application is fabricated from the
   221    major's io-inferred, head-normalised type, scope-guarded, certified
   222    against the constructor's telescope, type-checked against the major's
   223    type, and equated to the major by proof irrelevance (the last `DefEq`
   224    premise: the bridge builds it from `proofIrrel`'s two arms). -/

== whitepaper/Fragment/Sound.lean#L77-L84
    77  /-- **Certificates give fit**: a spine whose arguments are typed against
    78  the telescope's domains (each argument's inferred type definitionally
    79  equal to the binder domain it meets) fits the telescope semantically —
    80  the folded `Certs` walk of `Red.iota`, made semantic. -/
    81  theorem teleFit_of_certs {Γ : List Expr} {ρ : Nat → V} (hs : Sat m.M φ Γ ρ) :
    82      ∀ {T : Expr} {spine tys doms : List Expr},
    83        WellDenoted m.M φ ρ T → (∀ a ∈ spine, WellDenoted m.M φ ρ a) →
    84        Expr.piDomains T spine = some doms → tys.length = doms.length →

== whitepaper/Fragment/Sound.lean#L201-L206
   201  /-- ι: the two certificates give the two telescope fits, the three
   202  comparisons give their semantic forms (the residual's index
   203  expressions are well-denoted because the residual is,
   204  `WellDenoted_piResidual`), the reduced major's denotation replaces the
   205  argument's, and the environment's `RecRuleLaw` gives the equation and
   206  the reduct's invariant. -/

== whitepaper/Fragment/EnvModel.lean#L102-L161
   102  /-- **The ι law of one recursor rule** (con-leche's `RecRuleLaw`,
   103  `ConLeche/Model/Annot/Laws.lean`), stated on **values**.  For the
   104  recursor `c` (stored as `ci`, with `numParams` parameters,
   105  `numBefore = numParams + numMotives + numMinors` arguments before the
   106  indices, the major at `majorIdx`) and its rule `rl` for the
   107  constructor stored as `cij`: whenever values `xs` up to the major,
   108  together with the constructor's set applied to values `ys` as the
   109  major, fit the recursor's telescope, `ys` fit the constructor's
   110  telescope, and the three comparisons of `Red.iota` hold in their
   111  semantic form — the constructor's levels evaluate as the recursor's
   112  last `usj.length` ones, its parameters ARE the recursor's, and the
   113  index expressions of its residual type (`piBodyV`: the family at the
   114  constructor's parameters and index expressions, read under the fields)
   115  denote the recursor's index arguments — then the recursor's set
   116  applied to the spine is the rule's right-hand side's set applied to
   117  the parameters, motives, minors and the fields; and the right-hand
   118  side is well-denoted, with a well-formed application chain along
   119  those values (which is what makes the reduct well-denoted,
   120  `WellDenoted_mkAppN_of_spineOk`).
   121  
   122  Values rather than terms so that the law mentions the model only at
   123  the STORED terms (the two types and the right-hand side): extending
   124  the environment by a fresh constant then leaves every old law intact
   125  (`Install.lean`), where a law over arbitrary argument terms would have
   126  to be re-proved for the terms that mention the new name.  The ι rule's
   127  soundness converts its term-level certificates to this form
   128  (`Tele.lean`).
   129  
   130  **Part 2's obligation, named.**  Where the family is a *type*, the
   131  law follows from the **fixpoint's inversion** alone: the recursor's
   132  fit puts the major — a tagged tuple of the fields — in the family at
   133  the RECURSOR's parameters and indices, and a member of the family
   134  built by `rl.ctor` has its fields in the constructor's field
   135  telescope at THOSE parameters, which is what the right-hand side's β
   136  steps need and what the recursion equation of the model's recursor is
   137  stated over.  Where the family is a *proposition* the major denotes
   138  the point and the fits say only that the fibre is inhabited; the
   139  three comparisons then relate the fields `ys` to the recursor's own
   140  parameters and indices, and the subsingleton criterion makes the
   141  recursor's value at the point the value at those fields. -/
   142  def RecRuleLaw (M : Name → List Nat → V) (c : Name) (ci : ConstInfo)
   143      (numParams numBefore majorIdx : Nat) (rl : RecRule) (cij : ConstInfo) : Prop :=
   144    ∀ (φ : Name → Nat) (ρ : Nat → V) (us usj : List Level) (xs ys : List V),
   145      us.length = ci.lparams.length → usj.length = cij.lparams.length →
   146      xs.length = majorIdx → ys.length = numParams + rl.nfields →
   147      TeleFitV M φ ρ (ci.type.instL ci.lparams us)
   148        (xs ++ [appList (M rl.ctor (usj.map (Level.eval φ))) ys]) →
   149      TeleFitV M φ ρ (cij.type.instL cij.lparams usj) ys →
   150      usj.map (Level.eval φ) = (us.drop (us.length - usj.length)).map (Level.eval φ) →
   151      ys.take numParams = xs.take numParams →
   152      (∀ (B : Expr) (ρ' : Nat → V) (I : Name) (lsI : List Level) (rps ridx : List Expr),
   153        piBodyV ρ (cij.type.instL cij.lparams usj) ys = some (B, ρ') →
   154        B = Expr.mkAppN (.const I lsI) (rps ++ ridx) → rps.length = numParams →
   155        ∀ p ∈ (ridx.map (interp M φ ρ')).zip (xs.drop numBefore), p.1 = p.2) →
   156      appList (M c (us.map (Level.eval φ)))
   157          (xs ++ [appList (M rl.ctor (usj.map (Level.eval φ))) ys])
   158        = appList (interp M φ ρ (rl.rhs.instL ci.lparams us))
   159            (xs.take numBefore ++ ys.drop numParams) ∧
   160      WellDenoted M φ ρ (rl.rhs.instL ci.lparams us) ∧
   161      SpineOk (interp M φ ρ (rl.rhs.instL ci.lparams us)) (xs.take numBefore ++ ys.drop numParams)

   438      (n : Name) (cv : ConstantVal) (mI rP : Nat) (rl : RecRule) :

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L225-L244
   225    | rescueK {d : Nat} {major tm tmaj fab tf : Expr} {recName : Name}
   226        {cv : ConstantVal} {mI rP : Nat} {rl : RecRule} {cvj : ConstantVal}
   227        {cnP cnF : Nat} {T : Name} {tus ust : List Level} {cvT : ConstantVal}
   228        {caps : IndCaps} :

== ConLeche/Kernel/Core.lean#L1852-L1881
  1852      | .letE ty v b => do
  1853        -- The body is annotated *with the value transparent* — nanoda's
  1854        -- `infer_let` instantiates the body with the value and recurses
  1855        -- (the official kernel gets the same transparency from valued
  1856        -- let-fvars in its local context).  ConLeche fvars carry no value,
  1857        -- so the body is annotated as its zeta reduct; an opened opaque
  1858        -- variable was tried and rejects real streams (elaborated `let`
  1859        -- bodies rely on the value definitionally — see DESIGN.md).
  1860        --
  1861        -- Task #217 (audit follow-up #206-S1): the official `infer_let`
  1862        -- triple — `ensure_sort_core(infer(type))`, `infer(val)`,
  1863        -- `is_def_eq(val_type, type)` — runs HERE, on the annotated
  1864        -- annotation and the annotated value, before the reduct is taken.
  1865        --
  1866        -- Task #161 item C2 dropped it as redundant with `inferBody`'s
  1867        -- own `.letE` clause.  That was wrong: this clause returns the ζ
  1868        -- reduct, so the stored term is let-free and `inferBody`'s
  1869        -- `.letE` arm never sees a `letE` node the driver produced —
  1870        -- `def x : Nat := let y : Nat := Bool.true; Nat.zero` was
  1871        -- accepted where the official kernel rejects ("(kernel)
  1872        -- let-declaration type mismatch").  The annotation pass is the
  1873        -- only pass that meets a `letE`, so it is where the triple must
  1874        -- run.
  1875        let ty' ← r.annotate depth ty
  1876        let _ ← ensureSort r env depth (← r.infer depth ty')
  1877        let v' ← r.annotate depth v
  1878        let tv ← r.infer depth v'
  1879        unless ← r.defeq depth tv ty' do
  1880          throw (.invalid "let value type mismatch")
  1881        r.annotate depth (b.instantiate1 v)

== ConLeche/Cached/Installed.lean#L450-L455
   450  def checkDecls (mode : CheckMode) (pins : List NatOpPinSet)
   451      (ds : Array Declaration) :
   452      Except (CheckError × Nat) Env := do
   453    let (p, _) ← (ds.foldlM (annotDeclStep mode pins) (0, mkFEnv Env.empty, #[])) {}
   454    checkPendingList mode p.2.1 p.2.2.toList
   455    pure p.2.1.env

== ConLeche/Cached/Installed.lean#L350-L361
   350  The driver's check phase — the in-thread loop or a pool of workers —
   351  runs `checkRecord` on every record.  Its result is the record's own
   352  evidence: on an accept the `GroupChecked` fact of that record, on a
   353  failure the error tagged with the record's fold position, the tag
   354  `checkPendingList` gives.  A worker hands back exactly this (a `Nat`
   355  and an erased proof, or the error), so the thread that computed a
   356  check is irrelevant to what it proves, and the results of any number
   357  of workers, in whatever order they finished, are assembled into
   358  `∀ i, GroupChecked mode e i` by `collectChecks` — a walk over the
   359  results in record order, which is also what makes the verdict of a
   360  pool the verdict of the walk `checkPendingList`: the first failing
   361  record in fold order.  Nothing here is `IO`. -/

== ConLeche/Verify/Cached/MainC.lean#L50-L53
    50  theorem checkDecls_sound (hμ : μ.verifiedChecks = true)
    51      {ds : Array Declaration} {env' : Env}
    52      (h : checkDecls μ pins ds = .ok env') :
    53      Nonempty (EnvModelM V μ env') := by

== ConLeche/Semantics/Syntax.lean#L66-L90
    66  inductive AnnotTerm where
    67    /-- de Bruijn index -/
    68    | bvar (i : Nat)
    69    /-- `Sort u` at a concrete level -/
    70    | sort (u : Nat)
    71    /-- a built-in constant at a concrete level instantiation -/
    72    | const (c : BConst) (us : List Nat)
    73    /-- application -/
    74    | app (f a : AnnotTerm)
    75    /-- `fun (_ : ty) => body`, where `body`'s **type** has sort `u` —
    76    the codomain numeral `interp` dispatches on (tier B's F4; the
    77    #152 resolution made it derivable, and `Annotates.lam` caches it) -/
    78    | lam (u : Nat) (ty body : AnnotTerm)
    79    /-- `(_ : ty) → body`, with `ty`'s sort `u` and `body`'s sort `v` -/
    80    | pi (u v : Nat) (ty body : AnnotTerm)
    81    /-- `@Eq _ lhs rhs`; no annotation, and no type slot either, as in
    82    `Term` (task #237) -/
    83    | eqE (lhs rhs : AnnotTerm)
    84    /-- first field of a pair -/
    85    | fst (e : AnnotTerm)
    86    /-- second field of a pair -/
    87    | snd (e : AnnotTerm)
    88    /-- the canonical (irrelevant) proof of a derivable equation -/
    89    | prf
    90    deriving Repr, Inhabited

== ConLeche/Model/Annot/Bit.lean#L153-L156
   153  @[expose] def denoteMeta (acval : Name → (Name → Nat) → AnnotTerm)
   154      (env : Env) (φ : Name → Nat) :
   155      (d : Nat) → Expr → Option AnnotTerm
   156    | _, .sort u => some (.sort (u.eval φ))

== ConLeche/Semantics/Interp.lean#L150-L160
   150  noncomputable def interp : (Nat → V) → AnnotTerm → V
   151    | ρ, .bvar i => ρ i
   152    | _, .sort u => univ u
   153    | _, .const c us => bval V c us
   154    | ρ, .app f a => SetTheory.app (interp ρ f) (interp ρ a)
   155    | ρ, .lam v A b => lamR v (interp ρ A) fun x => interp (cons x ρ) b
   156    | ρ, .pi _ v A B => piR v (interp ρ A) fun x => interp (cons x ρ) B
   157    | ρ, .eqE a b => eqv (interp ρ a) (interp ρ b)
   158    | ρ, .fst e => sfst (interp ρ e)
   159    | ρ, .snd e => ssnd (interp ρ e)
   160    | _, .prf => pt

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L576-L587
   576  inductive Certs (env : Env) : Nat → Bool → Expr → List Expr → Prop where
   577    | nil {d : Nat} {lic : Bool} {T : Expr} : Certs env d lic T []
   578    | skip {d : Nat} {lic : Bool} {ty body arg : Expr} {mb : BinderMeta}
   579        {rest : List Expr} :
   580        lic = true → mb.pw.isNever = true →
   581        Certs env d lic (body.instantiate1 arg) rest →
   582        Certs env d lic (.forallE ty body mb) (arg :: rest)
   583    | cert {d : Nat} {lic : Bool} {ty body arg ta : Expr} {mb : BinderMeta}
   584        {rest : List Expr} :
   585        Infer env .io d arg ta → DefEq env d ta ty →
   586        Certs env d lic (body.instantiate1 arg) rest →
   587        Certs env d lic (.forallE ty body mb) (arg :: rest)

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L590-L594
   590  inductive DefEqList (env : Env) : Nat → List Expr → List Expr → Prop where
   591    | nil {d : Nat} : DefEqList env d [] []
   592    | cons {d : Nat} {a b : Expr} {as bs : List Expr} :
   593        DefEq env d a b → DefEqList env d as bs →
   594        DefEqList env d (a :: as) (b :: bs)

== ConLeche/Denotes.lean#L132-L135

   133  the module docstring. -/

   135      (BVarIdx → V) → Expr → V → Prop

== ConLeche/Denotes.lean#L270-L290
   270  structure Model (V : Type w) [SetTheory V] (env : Env) where
   271    /-- the set a constant denotes, per level assignment -/
   272    cval : Name → (LevelParam → Nat) → V
   273    /-- every stored constant is a member of what its type denotes, at
   274    every level assignment (and every variable environment — the type
   275    is closed) -/
   276    mem : ∀ c ∈ env.consts, ∀ (φ : LevelParam → Nat) (ρ : BVarIdx → V),
   277      ∃ T, Denotes cval env φ ρ c.toConstantVal.type T ∧ cval c.name φ ∈ˢ T
   278    /-- whatever the built-in `False` denotes is the empty set -/
   279    false_empty : ∀ (φ : LevelParam → Nat) (ρ : BVarIdx → V) (F : V),
   280      Denotes cval env φ ρ (.const falseName []) F → F = empty
   281    /-- whatever the built-in `Eq` denotes is set equality: at a type `A`
   282    of the universe the level `u` names, and two of its members `a` and
   283    `b`, `@Eq.{u} A a b` denotes the truth value of `a = b`.  The three
   284    membership premises are the graph's domains — `Eq`'s denotation is a
   285    three-fold graph over `univ (Level.eval φ u)`, then over `A`, then
   286    over `A` again, and a graph read off its domain says nothing -/
   287    eq_equality : ∀ (u : Level) (φ : LevelParam → Nat) (ρ : BVarIdx → V) (E A a b : V),
   288      Denotes cval env φ ρ (.const eqName [u]) E →
   289      A ∈ˢ univ (Level.eval φ u) → a ∈ˢ A → b ∈ˢ A →
   290      app (app (app E A) a) b = eqv a b

   225        denoteMeta acval env φ d e = some ta →
   226        Expr.fvarsBelow d e → e.looseBVarsBounded 0 = true →
   227        ∀ ρ : Nat → V, WellDenotedV V ρ ta →
   228          Denotes (cvalOf (V := V) acval) env φ ρ (closeN d e) (interp V ρ ta) := by
